profile.stagger_pattern: ACFR verbatim: 'Policy-making and legislative authority are vested in the governing council consisting of the mayor and seven other members... Council members serve four-year staggered terms, with an election held every two years. The mayor is also elected to serve a four-year term. Four of the council members are elected by district. The mayor and the three remaining council members are elected at large.' Observed split: Wards I-IV all elected together in Nov 2019 and Nov 2023 (terms Jan 2020-Dec 2023, Jan 2024-Dec 2027); Mayor + the three At Large seats elected together in Nov 2021 and Nov 2025 (terms Jan 2022-Dec 2025, Jan 2026-Dec 2029). At Large seats are unnumbered and run as a single group, top three elected.

run_log.detail: REGISTRY ENTRY DEAD: the Georgia entry's Courier Herald pattern 'courierheraldtoday.com/wp-content/uploads/{YYYY}/{MM}/CH-{Month DD, YYYY}.pdf' returns HTTP 404 for every date tested (Nov 2019, Nov 2021, Nov 2023, Nov 2025). CORRECTED PATTERN, verified working: 'courierheraldtoday.com/wp-content/uploads/{YYYY}/{MM}/CH-{Month}-{D}-{YYYY}.pdf' -- hyphen-separated, no comma, no spaces, no leading zero on the day (e.g. .../2025/11/CH-November-6-2025.pdf, .../2025/12/CH-December-4-2025.pdf). Some issues carry a '-1' suffix (CH-October-23-2025-1.pdf). ARCHIVE DEPTH: the WordPress upload archive begins in 2024 -- every 2023 and earlier date probed 404s, so this source cannot reach the 2019, 2021 or 2023 cycles. The /e-editions/ page is a subscriber portal (Pelcro paywall SDK) with no PDF links. Also confirmed dead: laurenscoga.org/258/Election-Results 302-redirects straight into results.enr.clarityelections.com/GA/Laurens/ (robots-blocked); laurenscoga.org returns 403 to curl. gacities.com/gma-cities-districts/dublin/24376 fetched fine but is STALE -- it still lists Richard Mascarro, who left the council 2025-12-31, and omits Brandon Chain.

Established from the FY2023 ACFR transmittal letter (verbatim: 'the governing council consisting of the mayor and seven other members... Council members serve four-year staggered terms, with an election held every two years... Four of the council members are elected by district. The mayor and the three remaining council members are elected at large.') plus observed ballots. Wards I-IV run together (2019, 2023); Mayor + the three unnumbered At Large seats run together as a single group, top three elected (2021, 2025). GEORGIA UNOPPOSED-SEAT QUESTION (raised mid-flight): Dublin's record is consistent with unopposed seats not reaching the ballot. WGXA's 2019 election-night piece says verbatim 'The City of Dublin is voting on two city council seats' and lists only Ward 2 and Ward 4, yet the FY2019->FY2020 ACFR snapshots show all four wards turning over on the same January 2020 boundary and the January 4 2024 minutes administer the oath to 'CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS WARD[S] 1,2,3 and 4' together. Likewise no mayoral race appears anywhere in the Courier Herald's November 6 2025 election coverage even though Joshua Kight's four-year term expired December 2025 and he is mayor in 2026. Operational consequence adopted here: a Dublin seat absent from a November results report was treated as 'unopposed and seated', NOT as missing data, and the holder was carried forward on ACFR evidence rather than filed as a gap. STATUTORY BASIS (supplied mid-run by the Milledgeville agent, adopted): O.C.G.A. §21-2-285(c) and §21-2-291 -- no election is held where no candidate is opposed, and the unopposed candidate is certified elected. This makes the treatment above the correct default for Georgia, not a workaround. Zero gaps were filed for absent-from-ballot seats.

THE SPINE OF THIS CITY IS THE ACFR SERIES, exactly as the mid-flight note predicted. cityofdublin.org/departments/finance links a complete unbroken run FY2012-FY2025 as direct PDFs. Filenames are NOT uniform -- three distinct conventions coexist and constructed guesses ('2019_Audit_for_City_of_Dublin.pdf', 'City of Dublin - 2019 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.pdf') all 404; the finance page must be scraped for the real hrefs. Note FY2019 and FY2013 embed a %C2%A0 non-breaking space in the filename. FORMAT CHANGE MID-SERIES: FY2012-FY2021 present the roster as an unlabeled organization chart under a 'CITY COUNCIL' heading, listing seven names with '(Mayor Pro Tem)' and '(Chairman of Council)' annotations but NO ward/at-large labels; FY2022 onward present a labeled 'Elected Officials' table ('Council Member - Ward I', '- At Large') but DROP the officer annotations. Each report is a fiscal-year-end (June 30) snapshot, not a publication-date snapshot -- proven by FY2021 still showing Phil Best as mayor months after Joshua Kight took office. All extracted locally with pdftotext -layout; every name below is verbatim from that extraction. The CVIOG/TED mirror (ted.cviog.uga.edu/financial-documents/node/{id}) was tried as a cross-check per the mid-run tip; its fulltext-search URL returned a 16KB shell with no Dublin node links, and it would in any case mirror the same city-issued PDFs already held, so it was not pursued further. Dublin's budget documents were also checked as a seat-label source (Budget Listing_FY2022.pdf, HTTP 200, 294KB) -- unlike Milledgeville's, Dublin's budget listing contains no officials roster at all, so it does not resolve the FY2019-FY2021 seat-label problem.

2019 cycle, WGXA (dated 2019-11-05) verbatim: 'Dublin city council Ward 2: Christopher Smith / Dublin city council Ward 4: Bill Brown, III' with the pre-election field 'Ward 2: Jason Keyton, Michael Paul Martin, Christopher Smith; Ward 4: Bill Brown III, Jerome Pullen'. 2021 cycle, WGXA qualifying list (dated 2021-08-24) verbatim: 'Jerry Davis - Mayor / Joshua E. Knight - Mayor / Sara Kolbie - At large / Richard Mascaro- At large / Albert "Ratt" Brown Jr -At large / Tess Godfrey - At large / Brandon Chain- At large' (note 'Knight' is WGXA's misspelling of Kight). 2025 cycle, Courier Herald November 6 2025 PDF verbatim: 'Chain received 770 votes, 11 more than Lanier, to pick up the third at-large Dublin City Council seat during Tuesday's election. Incumbents Tess Godfrey, who was the lead vote getter with 1,247, and Sara Kolbie, with 1,129, will be returning to their seats.' Also names 'Rae S. Bloodworth (589), J. Roy Rowland' and confirms 'Chain ran with Godfrey and Kolbie four years ago.' 2023 cycle: no vote record located anywhere; the seating is instead established by the January 4 2024 organizational minutes, whose roll call names all seven members, and by the Courier Herald January 4 2024 agenda listing 'Administration of the oath of office for City Council Members for Wards 1,2,3 and 4'.

THREE mid-term changes found, all invisible in election records. (1) MAYORAL VACANCY: Phil Best, Sr. retired at the end of June 2021 after 22 years as mayor; the council installed Julie Driger as INTERIM MAYOR from July 2021 -- WGXA verbatim, 2021-11-18: 'Kight will replace interim Mayor Julie Driger who has sat in the Mayoral seat since July.' Driger was not a sitting council member at the time (she is a former Dublin councilmember of 26 years who retired in 2015), so the Mayor Pro Tem succession was NOT used. Her last day was 2021-11-18, when Kight was sworn in at the council meeting -- i.e. Kight took office three weeks after the November 2 election rather than the following January, because he was filling an unexpired term. (2) AT LARGE VACANCY: Jerry Davis is present in the FY2020 ACFR snapshot (2020-06-30) and absent from FY2021 (2021-06-30); Gary Johnson -- who had left Ward II in January 2020 -- reappears in the FY2021 snapshot in his place. This is an appointment to an unexpired at-large term, dated only to the window 2020-07-01/2021-06-30; searches for a Davis resignation or a Johnson appointment vote returned nothing. Davis went on to run for mayor in November 2021 and is described by WGXA as a 'Former Dublin city councilmen'. (3) WARD II TURNOVER at the 2019 cycle: Gary Johnson did not appear among the Ward 2 candidates, so his seat opened without a resignation. CAVEATS, filed here rather than as gaps: Best's 2021-06-30 exit date is the month boundary implied by 'since July', not a dated resignation letter; Davis's 2021-06-30 exit and Johnson's 2021-06-30 entry are the latest-possible boundary consistent with the two ACFR snapshots and are marked low confidence; the FY2022 ACFR renders Ward II as 'Chris Jones', a clerical error for Chris Smith (FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 and the January 2024 roll call all read 'Chris Smith') -- recorded as a name variant, NOT as a second person.

Seat count holds at 7 council + mayor in every year 2019-2026; no redistricting or seat-count change in the window. Ward assignment for 2019-2021 is INFERRED, since the FY2018-FY2021 ACFR org charts list seven names without seat labels: Bennie Jones (Ward I), Paul Griggs (Ward III) and Bill Brown III (Ward IV) carry forward unchanged into the labeled FY2022+ tables; Gary Johnson is placed in Ward II because Christopher Smith won the Ward 2 race in November 2019 and replaces exactly Johnson between the FY2019 and FY2020 snapshots; the residual three (Jerry Davis, Gerald Smith, Curtis Edwards) are therefore the three At Large seats, and all three vacate together at the 2021-12-31 boundary when the November 2021 at-large group winners take office. This is elimination against a labeled later table, not free inference, but the at-large trio is recorded at medium confidence for that reason. Dublin's three At Large seats are UNNUMBERED -- no posts, no positions; candidates run as one group and the top three are elected -- so all three carry the identical seat_label 'At Large' and are distinguished only by person. INTERNAL OFFICERS: Dublin elects BOTH a Mayor Pro Tempore and a Chairman of Council at its January organizational meeting (both appear as separate agenda items in the Courier Herald's January 4 2024 agenda). Only the Mayor Pro Tem is recorded as the vice_mayor seat. Chairman of Council observations, for the record: Curtis Edwards (FY2018, FY2019), Bennie Jones (FY2020, FY2021), Rich Mascaro (elected 2024-01-04, minutes verbatim: 'Mascaro as Chairman of Council'), Paul Griggs (2026, city website). CONTRADICTION RESOLVED: a search summary asserted 'Bennie Jones serves as Council Member for Ward II, Paul Griggs as Council Member for Ward IV' -- this is fabricated; every primary document (FY2022-FY2025 ACFRs and the live city website) reads Jones = Ward I, Griggs = Ward III. A second search summary guessed Rae Bloodworth took the third 2025 at-large seat; the Courier Herald text says Chain, by 11 votes over Lanier. Both were discarded in favour of locally extracted text.

20 tenure rows across 9 seats (Mayor, Wards 1-4, three At Large, Mayor Pro Tem) x 8 years. 69 of 72 seat-years sourced; 3 seat-years in gaps, all of them the Mayor Pro Tem office in 2022, 2023 and 2024. No lawfully-vacant seat-years found.
